reason: PR #192 exact Head bccb43e6817c5c258dbfc35fd161db6cfd43cbe1 reproduces PVEP Attested Evidence failure on both Linux and Windows, including a rerun of the same failed jobs, while the base-owned command set is a fixed node -e selftest and the trusted runner emits no child failure details. Independent reproduction proves the current runner inherits ambient NODE_OPTIONS because sanitizedEnvironment filters only secret-like names; an invalid inherited NODE_OPTIONS makes the same node -e selftest exit 1. This authorization permits a bottom-layer hardening of the existing PVEP trusted runner so base-owned commands execute under an explicit deterministic environment contract and failed child execution emits safe machine-verifiable diagnostics. It does not authorize changes to PR #192, command sets, workflows, dependencies, product code, or a second verification framework.

ossFit.basis: The repair modifies the already-authorized PVEP base-owned runner and its contract tests only, using Node.js core child_process/environment primitives. No replacement verifier, runner framework, signing system, command executor, or dependency is introduced.

requiredGenericCapability.name: deterministicTrustedCommandEnvironmentAndFailureEvidence
requirements: Base-owned command execution must not inherit ambient Node process-control variables such as NODE_OPTIONS or NODE_PATH.

The child environment must be constructed from an explicit minimal cross-platform allowlist required for process discovery and temporary-directory operation; arbitrary repository, workflow, runner, and secret environment variables must not flow through by default.
Environment key matching must account for Windows case-insensitive environment semantics.
The trusted command set remains the sole authority for executable, argv, expected exit code, generated roots, and artifact declarations.
A failed child command must still produce the existing evidence JSON with verificationStatus VERIFIED_FAIL before the runner exits nonzero.

Failure diagnostics written to stderr must be machine-verifiable and safe: include commandId, expected/observed exit code, signal or spawn error code, and stdout/stderr digests, but never raw child stdout/stderr or secret-bearing environment values.
Workspace Head and dirty-worktree fail-closed checks remain unchanged.
No retry, timeout relaxation, ignored failure, fallback command, shell execution, or candidate-controlled override is permitted.

requiredCausalRed: With an inherited invalid NODE_OPTIONS value, the current trusted runner allows the ambient variable to alter its base-owned node child and the trusted command fails.
A deliberately failing trusted child currently leaves GitHub logs without a safe structured child-failure reason even though the evidence file records the fields.
requiredGreen: The same trusted command passes when the parent process contains hostile or invalid NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH because those variables are not inherited by the child.
Arbitrary ambient variables and secret-like variables are absent from the child environment unless explicitly allowlisted as platform-critical.
A deliberate child exit failure remains fail-closed and emits safe structured diagnostics with no raw stdout/stderr.
Existing base-owned runner, exact-Head, workspace cleanliness, trusted command-set ownership, evidence digest, and subject binding tests remain GREEN on Linux and Windows.
